case.title: 'buy from' (vendor) starts before 'kiosk' (public_tap); the earliest start position decides

submissions.open_text: Queue times exceed an hour most mornings.
submissions.voice_transcript: We buy from the kiosk near the chief's office.

submissions.open_text: The hand pump handle broke last month.

case.why: 'buy from' starts at character 3 and 'kiosk' starts later, so the earliest keyword is 'buy from' and the source heard is vendor. Vendor differs from the form's public_tap, so the check fires. An implementation that prefers the most specific keyword, scans keywords in list order (public_tap before vendor), or skips verb phrases would pick kiosk and stay silent. The companion's open_text shares no content words with the target's.

review: Corrected in review: kiosks sell water by the jerrycan and the form's label is 'public tap or kiosk', so this is consistent; 'buy from' says vendor only when no source is named.
